title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pages 7, 5, next page): this is a 'surgery' toolkit for conformal surfaces, here the gluing (recollement) and capping of holes. Let X be a compact Riemann surface with boundary and C a boundary component. C carries only a real-analytic structure. Grothendieck observes the following.
(1) Capping C by a disc D (forming the closed-up surface X' = X ∪_C D) is the same as giving C a real projective structure: an RP^1-structure isomorphic to the standard one on ∂D. The reason is that Aut(D) = PSL(2,R) acts on ∂D by real projective transformations. So the gluing is determined exactly up to Aut(D) by a projective structure on C. The regularity properties of that projective structure, relative to the given real-analytic structure, mirror the regularity of C viewed as a curve in X'.
(2) Choosing a point a ∈ D∖C (a 'centre') amounts to reducing the structure group from PGL(2,R) = GL(2,R)/R* to its maximal compact subgroup O(2)/±1, the stabiliser of a in the disc model. Concretely, this is a 'toric/torsorial' structure on C: C becomes a torsor under the circle group, i.e. a parametrisation by S^1 up to rotation. Equivalently it is a 'linear' structure of D on ∂D = C.
(3) There is then a canonical embedding D ⊂ T_{X',a}. Take the unique conformal map f from D to a round disc in T_a X' with f(a) = 0 and df_a = id (unique by Schwarz's lemma). The radius is the conformal radius, which gives a disc in T_a well defined in the infinitesimal conformal structure.
The page ends by announcing a Proposition, finished on the next page. It is an equivalence between two categories:
- (a) compact conformal surfaces with boundary, with a chosen boundary component C carrying a (rectifiable / real-analytic-compatible) circle-torsor structure;
- (b) conformal surfaces X' with a pointed disc (D, a) ⊂ Int X' whose boundary is a rectifiable (analytic) curve.
The next page adds that, for fixed (X', a), the discs around a form an R*_+-torsor under homotheties in T_{X',a}.
In modern terms this is the correspondence used in Segal's CFT, Vafa, Huang and Kontsevich/ADKP: a boundary circle parametrised up to rotation, plus its complement, corresponds to a filled-in disc with a marked centre. Equivalently, Diff(S^1)/S^1 corresponds to normalised univalent functions via conformal welding (Kirillov 1987). The projective-structure step corresponds to Diff(S^1)/PSL(2,R) (universal Teichmüller-type space).
errors: Not every real projective structure on a circle can be capped. RP^1-structures on S^1 have hyperbolic, parabolic, elliptic and n-fold covering types; only the one isomorphic to ∂D (developing map a degree-1 diffeomorphism onto RP^1) yields a disc. The page leaves this restriction implicit.
O(2)/±1 contains orientation-reversing elements. Once C has the boundary orientation from X, the relevant stabiliser is SO(2)/±1 inside PSL(2,R); this is harmless but imprecise.

'D ⊂ T_{X',a}' is an embedding as a round disc via the normalised Riemann map, not an inclusion of subsets. The radius (conformal radius) is meaningful only up to the R*_+ ambiguity of the conformal structure on T_a, which the next page addresses.

The regularity hypotheses (rectifiable versus real-analytic) are left vague. For general Jordan curves, conformal welding needs quasisymmetric or similar conditions, and uniqueness can fail for non-removable curves.

ideas.what: Real projective structure on a boundary circle is equivalent to a way of capping the hole by a disc (Aut(D)=PSL(2,R) acting projectively on ∂D)
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures on S^1 / capping boundary via conformal welding; Diff(S^1)/PSL(2,R)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Möbius action on the circle); welding viewpoint: Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen; Kirillov (1987) in the Diff(S^1) setting

ideas.what: A centre a in the cap corresponds to reducing the structure group PGL(2,R) to its maximal compact PO(2), i.e. a circle-torsor (parametrisation up to rotation) on C
ideas.modern_name: Diff(S^1)/S^1 ≅ normalised univalent functions; parametrised boundaries in Segal's category

ideas.what: Canonical embedding of a disc with centre a as a round disc in T_{X',a} via the normalised Riemann map; discs around a form an R*_+-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Conformal radius / local coordinate at a puncture (jets of local coordinates)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarz lemma, conformal radius); used systematically by Huang, Vafa, Segal

ideas.what: Proposed equivalence of categories: surfaces with a parametrised (up to rotation) boundary component versus closed-up surfaces with an embedded pointed disc
ideas.modern_name: Sewing / plumbing correspondence underlying Segal's conformal field theory and the Virasoro uniformisation of moduli
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal; Vafa; Huang (vertex operator algebra sewing); Kontsevich, Arbarello–De Concini–Kac–Procesi, Beilinson–Schechtman (late 1980s)

missed.claim: In 1983–84 Grothendieck formulates the dictionary between boundary data and filled discs as a structure-group reduction ladder. Real-analytic circle → real projective structure (PGL(2,R)) ↔ capping disc. Then → PO(2)-structure (circle torsor) ↔ capping disc with centre. Then → embedding in the tangent space at the centre. This is precisely the geometry behind Kirillov's Diff(S^1)/S^1 ↔ univalent functions and Segal's category of Riemann surfaces with parametrised boundary, a few years before those works. He organises it as a categorical equivalence that serves as a surgery calculus for conformal surfaces.
missed.quote: le choix d'un point de D \ C équivaut à celui d'une structure torique sur C compatible avec la structure de droite projective réelle (i.e. une réduction du groupe structural ... Gl(2,R)/R* au sous-groupe compact maximal O(2)/±1)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, independent formulation of the CFT sewing formalism phrased via G-structure reductions on the boundary. It supports a historical claim that Grothendieck's 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' (linked to dessins and Teichmüller towers) anticipated Segal-type gluing. It may suggest viewing Segal's category through the PSL(2,R) to S^1 reduction ladder.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics itself is classical (Möbius action, Riemann maps, conformal radius). However, its organisation as a structure-group reduction ladder and a categorical equivalence for surgery on conformal surfaces anticipates Segal/Kirillov-style boundary parametrisation by several years. That is a notable, largely undocumented precursor, though not a new theorem.
